sections.title: Introduction and Translation Methodology
sections.summary: Khalifa presents this as the first English rendering of the Quran meanings by a Muslim Arab. He argues that translators have often partially translated or inconsistently rendered Islamic terms like 'Allah' and 'Al-Rahman,' leading to misunderstandings. Khalifa claims that 'Allah' means 'the God' in Arabic and should be fully translated, not treated as an untranslatable proper name used only by Muslims.

sections.title: Sura Al-Fatihah: Structure and Commentary
sections.summary: Khalifa presents the full text of Al-Fatihah (The Opener), the first chapter, and explains its seven verses as containing the essence of Islamic principles. He discusses why the opening statement 'Bismillah' is part of every sura except Al-Tawbah and claims computerized analysis shows that letter counts in the Quran are deliberately designed. He argues the opening verse is integral to each sura and that omitting it from Al-Tawbah is deliberate within a mathematical system.

sections.title: Sura Al-Baqarah: Believers, Disbelievers, and Hypocrites
sections.summary: Khalifa presents verses 1-29 from Al-Baqarah and discusses how the Quran categorizes people into three groups: the righteous (described in 3 verses), the disbelievers (2 verses), and hypocrites (13 verses). He interprets this disproportion as reflecting the subtlety and danger of hypocrisy. The author claims people can evaluate themselves against the stated criteria without needing external commentary.

sections.title: Qur'anic Initials and the A.L.M. System
sections.summary: Khalifa explains that 29 suras begin with mysterious letter combinations called Qur'anic initials, with A.L.M. appearing at the start of Al-Baqarah. He presents a computerized study claiming these letters form a mathematical system that confirms the Quran's recorded sequence and authenticity. The frequency distribution of A, L, and M across relevant suras allegedly supports the integrity of the Qur'anic text as transmitted.

sections.title: Linguistic Efficiency and Qur'anic Preservation
sections.summary: Khalifa presents evidence that the Quran contains verses conveying multiple compatible meanings simultaneously through careful word placement and the deliberate omission of punctuation marks. He discusses computational findings showing identical letter counts in parallel suras (such as 57 occurrences of Qaf in two different Qaf-initialed suras), arguing this demonstrates mathematical design impossible by human authorship. These patterns allegedly prove the Quran's divine origin and perfect preservation.
